obligations.seam: agents CLI <-> core daemon (Unix control socket)
obligations.behavior: On connect the CLI reads the core's API version and refuses an incompatible one with exit 2 and a message naming both versions; it never sends a request to an incompatible core.
obligations.source_text: Packaging of the seam is two packages: the TS core is published to npm and the Python 'agents' CLI to PyPI, each versioned and released on its own. The core runs as a supervised local daemon on Node >= 22 and exposes a versioned JSON API with an SSE event stream over a Unix socket; the JSON schemas in this repo are the source of truth for both, and the CLI checks the core's API version on connect and refuses an incompatible one with an environment error (exit 2).

obligations.seam: agents CLI <-> core daemon (Unix control socket)
obligations.behavior: When the socket is absent or refuses, every runs verb exits 2 with a remediation hint on stderr, nothing on stdout, and no traceback.
obligations.source_text: The 'agents' CLI gains the noun groups 'agents agents list|status' and 'agents runs submit|list|show|attach|steer|cancel|logs|result', built on agentfront, each with --json, an explain entry and the exit-code contract (0 ok, 1 user error, 2 environment error); the scaffold drift is fixed in the same change (prog name 'agents', template wording in learn/explain and AGENTS.override.md).

obligations.behavior: The core rejects a submit whose agent, harness or repo is not in the local allow-list, before any worker or sandbox is created, and the allow-list can only be changed by the operator's config file.
obligations.source_text: Dispatch authority defaults to deny and is enforced by the core, not by a prompt: in D1 the control socket is owner-only (mode 0600) and a submit must name an agent, harness and repo that appear in an explicit local allow-list, which ships empty.

obligations.seam: contract schemas <-> TS core and Python CLI
obligations.behavior: Every payload either side emits or accepts validates against the versioned JSON Schemas in contract/; a schema change bumps the API version.
obligations.source_text: The control-plane contract is a set of versioned JSON Schemas in this repo for agent, session, run, control action and event, with stable IDs, caller/owner, idempotency key, deadline, explicit terminal states (succeeded, failed, cancelled, timed_out, unknown), a transport-independent event cursor and a per-harness capability document; both the TS core and the Python CLI validate against the same files.

obligations.behavior: No AI-SDK, OpenShell or vendor-SDK type name appears in a schema, CLI output or event; harness-specific data is carried only in an opaque, documented extension field.
obligations.source_text: AI-SDK types never appear in the public contract: the JSON schemas, CLI output and event stream are harness-neutral, so swapping the Vercel AI SDK for another harness runtime leaves them unchanged (issue #2 comment 4 litmus test). The Python side keeps the 400-line file cap, and each runtime dependency beyond agentfront needs the user's approval.

obligations.behavior: The worker's PID, event log and cursor are on disk before the core acknowledges the submit, and the worker keeps writing its event log if the core dies.
obligations.source_text: culture-agents separates a per-run worker shim (PID/control socket, event cursor, pending operator question persisted on disk) from the control-plane daemon, so restarting the daemon reconnects to live runs instead of orphaning them (issue #2 comment 2 section 2; Acceptance Test 2).

obligations.behavior: After a restart the core reports a surviving worker's run from its on-disk event log, marks live control as unavailable for that run, and never terminates the worker.
obligations.source_text: After a daemon restart in D1, surviving per-run workers are left running and their state is reported from the on-disk event log; live control of those runs returns in D2.

obligations.seam: core daemon <-> run store on disk
obligations.behavior: A run's state shown to a caller is always derived from the run store or a live worker; when neither establishes the outcome the state is 'unknown'.
obligations.source_text: On a single host, 'agents runs submit' hands a task to a TS core daemon and returns a durable run ID; the run can be listed, shown, attached to as a live event stream, steered mid-run and cancelled, against real harnesses, with no chat server running; run state is stored on disk and read back truthfully after the daemon restarts.

obligations.behavior: The core holds an exclusive lock for its lifetime, removes a stale socket only after acquiring the lock, and a second instance exits 2 naming the running one.
obligations.source_text: The core daemon is single-instance per user: it takes an exclusive lock before binding the control socket, removes a stale socket left by a killed daemon, and a second start exits with an environment error naming the running instance.

obligations.behavior: An adapter declares its capabilities up front; the core refuses any control action outside them with a typed 'unsupported' error naming the capability and does not forward it to the harness.
obligations.source_text: Capability reporting is honest: each harness adapter declares whether it supports steer, cancel, resume and operator questions; a control action the harness cannot perform is refused with a typed 'unsupported' error naming the capability, never silently dropped or simulated.

obligations.behavior: Every harness process of a run starts inside an OpenShell sandbox created for that run and the sandbox is deleted when the run reaches a terminal state or is reported 'unknown'.
obligations.source_text: D1 runs each harness through the AI SDK harness adapters inside an NVIDIA OpenShell sandbox: culture-agents implements the AI SDK's sandbox-session interface on top of the official OpenShell TypeScript SDK (@ai-openshell/sdk), because no OpenShell provider for the AI SDK exists, and the OpenShell policy and credential providers, not environment scrubbing alone, bound what a run can reach.

obligations.behavior: The sandbox receives no GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN or SSH_AUTH_SOCK from the operator's environment, and a push to the repository's remote from inside it is denied by policy.
obligations.source_text: In D1 the core starts at most one active run per repository path and refuses a second with a typed 'busy' error; the harness never receives the operator's GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN or SSH_AUTH_SOCK, and a push to the remote is denied, enforced by the OpenShell sandbox policy and credential providers.

obligations.behavior: Code enters culture-agents only by citation; no commit, branch or tag is pushed to cultureagent or agent-lifecycle, and their published HTTP API, console scripts and import paths are unchanged.
obligations.source_text: D1 changes nothing in cultureagent or agent-lifecycle: their published contracts (bridge HTTP API /v1/invocations, result schema cultureagent.bridge.result/v1, console scripts, agent_lifecycle.runtime import paths) and all current consumers keep working, and code is cited into culture-agents, never moved out.

obligations.behavior: Each sibling change is made in a worktree under ../.worktrees.<repo>/ on a work-scoped branch and lands by PR; no command writes inside a primary sibling checkout.
obligations.source_text: Sibling-repo changes for this work are made only in dedicated per-repo worktrees on work-scoped branches and land through PRs; primary sibling checkouts, their uncommitted work and their current branches are never touched.

obligations.behavior: The npm package @culture.dev/agents-core publishes with provenance before the PyPI publish starts, and a failed npm publish leaves nothing published to PyPI.
obligations.source_text: The TS core is published to npm as @culture.dev/agents-core, following embeddings-tumbler's publish workflow (npm provenance via id-token, PyPI publish waits for npm so a failed npm publish leaves nothing published).

obligations.behavior: CI installs from the committed lockfile with a frozen install and fails if package.json holds a range for a runtime dependency.
obligations.source_text: Every npm dependency of the TS core is pinned to an exact version with a committed lockfile, and an upgrade of any @ai-sdk/* or vendor SDK package is its own PR that re-runs the live D1 acceptance stage.

obligations.behavior: A released version registers only verbs that work end to end, and its capability document lists every unbuilt capability as unsupported.
obligations.source_text: Because every merge to main publishes to PyPI, partial control-plane code reaches users before D1 is complete; each PR therefore keeps unfinished verbs out of the registered CLI or marks them '(planned)', and the published capability document never claims an unbuilt capability.

obligations.behavior: The npm package @culture.dev/agents publishes with provenance before the PyPI publish starts, and a failed npm publish leaves nothing published to PyPI.
